decision: Promotion is blocked by release gates, and unmeasured gates say [value]
why: 60-day delinquency cannot exist before 60 days; showing a projected number as if measured is how bad models ship.
alternative: A dashboard of offline metrics and a promote button.
value: Nothing unmeasured is reported as measured.

decision: Champion vs challenger is one approval-rate vs bad-rate curve that draws itself, with today's cut marked
why: The business trade-off is 'how many more good customers at the same risk'; one chart with the operating point answers it.
alternative: AUC and KS numbers side by side.
value: Non-specialists can read the case for the challenger.

decision: Challenger traffic is routed by a hash of the account, capped at 50% until gates pass
why: A customer must see the same model across applications; the cap limits blast radius.
value: Clean A/B comparison and consistent customer experience.

decision: Feature drift is shown as training vs last-7-days bars with PSI, and drift above 0.20 pauses the challenger
why: Drift is the earliest warning that a model's assumptions broke; the histogram shows where.
alternative: Alert on accuracy only, which lags by months.
value: Retraining starts from evidence, weeks before losses move.

decision: The retraining plan is proposed by an agent and scheduled by a person
why: The steps are routine but the timing affects the book; a person owns it.
value: Predictable model releases with a named owner.
